test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 17 Jun, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A salesman marks his good 64% above the cost price and gives a discount of 25% on them. Find the percentage of this gain or loss.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net Profit% = a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100, where a = **Markup%** and b = **Discount%** (negative).

Net Profit% = 64 − 25 − (64 × 25) ÷ 100

Net Profit% = 39 − (1600 ÷ 100)

Net Profit% = 39 − 16 = 23%.

Since the result is positive, it is a **23% gain**.

**∴ The correct answer is 23% gain.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → **Markup%** = 64%, **Discount%** = 25%.
Formulas: MP = CP × (100 + Markup%) ÷ 100 | SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100 | Gain% = (SP − CP) ÷ CP × 100
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/520aedd58a09537c668b0cdf096f545a90f6519bc1c077023ab3995b57099327.png] 
⇒ Let **Cost Price (CP)** = 100.
⇒ **Marked Price (MP)** = 100 + 64% of 100 = 164.
⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = 164 − 25% of 164 = 164 − (164 ÷ 4) = 164 − 41 = 123.
⇒ **Gain** = SP − CP = 123 − 100 = 23.
⇒ **Gain%** = (23 ÷ 100) × 100 = 23%.

**∴ The correct answer is 23% gain.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relation between CP, MP, Discount and Profit

The relationship is given by the formula: MP ÷ CP = (100 + Profit%) ÷ (100 − Discount%).

Successive Percentage Changes

When a value is increased by x% and then decreased by y%, the net change is (x − y − xy/100)%.</p
